import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_39/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_39/training_1.csv"

Source3_39_0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)
Source3_39_1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Operation 1: JOIN Source3_39_0 and Source3_39_1 on "movieId"
# According to the operation history, join on movieId columns of both tables
joined_df = pd.merge(Source3_39_0, Source3_39_1, on="movieId", how="inner")

# Operation 2: group_by Source3_39_1.movieId and aggregate avg(Source3_39_1.rating)
# Since after join, movieId is unique column, group by movieId and average rating
grouped = joined_df.groupby("movieId", as_index=False).agg({"rating": "mean"})

# Rename columns to match target schema exactly
# Target schema: ['movieId': integer, 'rating': float]
# movieId is already integer, rating is float by default after mean aggregation
grouped["movieId"] = grouped["movieId"].astype(int)
grouped["rating"] = grouped["rating"].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target path
target_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_39/target_multisource.csv"
grouped.to_csv(target_path, index=False)
